story_type: NASA engineer rides the back seat of an F/A-18: afterburner takeoff, roll and loop, cockpit camera
hook: A NASA engineer, upside down in an F/A-18 over the desert.
narration: This NASA engineer was upside down in an F/A-18, high over the California desert.
Julie Levri is a systems engineer at NASA Ames. NASA gave her a back seat ride as a reward for her work.
At Edwards, the pilot pushed the throttles into afterburner and the jet leapt off the runway.
Three hundred and fifty knots. Then a roll, right around the axis of the airplane.
In hard turns, blood is pushed away from the brain. A G suit squeezes the legs to push it back up.
Then the pilot warned her. A loop was next.
Straight up. Over the top, upside down. Then straight down, with the G's coming on.
[short pause] By the end, the ride had topped five G's.
outcome: The F/A-18 brought her back down safely onto the runway at Edwards.

location_card.place: NASA Armstrong Flight Research Center, Edwards, California

title: Engineer rides an F/A-18 through a loop
description:
On July 15, 2026, NASA Ames systems engineer Julie Levri flew in the back seat of an F/A-18 at NASA's Armstrong Flight Research Center in Edwards, California, as part of NASA's employee incentive flights: an afterburner takeoff, a roll and a loop.
